lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Rebuilt the diagnostics service's monitoring dashboards around per-sensor error budgets, cutting mean time to detect incidents from 40 to 12 minutes.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.

- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue while rewriting the shared logging library, onboarding two new hires and taking over the weekend on-call rotation, which removed the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
- Raised diagnostic accuracy on 1,200 held-out cases from 71% to 79% by fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Cut p95 latency of single-request edge inference by 40% by serving the INT8 engine with dynamic batching.
- Using grouped tool-use rollouts, a composite reward over accuracy, citation validity and call count, and a GRPO loop with a frozen SFT reference, reduced end-to-end latency 5%.
- Stabilised GRPO training on sparse rewards by sampling a single rollout per prompt, so each update used exactly one scored trajectory.
- Documented the triage branch's abstention rules and escalation paths for the on-call reviewers, who adopted them as the team's runbook.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Cut p95 tool-call latency from 900 ms to 600 ms, a 50% reduction, by caching tool results and reusing completed sub-agent answers.
- Raised the runtime's task-completion rate by 12% on the benchmark suite, from 71% to 83%, by retrying failed sub-agent calls with their partial context.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Upstreamed 8 citation and faithfulness metrics to an open-source research-agent framework, where they now run in the default benchmark for every release.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Traced 3 structural pipeline defects in stability, sourcing and parameter handling to their modules with layered instrumentation; each was fixed upstream.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Experience is not listed newest first.
items.because: The current order makes the timeline harder to scan.

items.says: “Adds” is present tense in a role that ended in July 2024.
items.because: It makes the past-tense role’s timeline inconsistent.

items.says: The line does not establish that the checks produced the three-day release cycle.
items.because: It gives no basis for attributing that result to the checks.

items.says: The operational result comes after a long sequence of activities.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the main impact.

items.says: “Removed the nightly backlogs” gives no before-and-after measure of backlog or dispatch delay.
items.because: The reader cannot judge the improvement’s scale.

items.says: Dynamic batching cannot account for the stated single-request latency reduction.
items.because: Batching benefits grouped requests, but can add waiting time to a single request.

items.says: The 5% end-to-end latency reduction does not identify the workflow measured.
items.because: A reader cannot tell which user or system path improved.

items.says: One scored rollout per prompt cannot provide the within-prompt comparisons GRPO uses.
items.because: Without multiple scored trajectories, the stated setup cannot provide the claimed GRPO stabilization.

items.says: “Stabilised” does not specify what became more stable.
items.because: The line gives no observable outcome, such as fewer failed runs or lower training variation.

items.says: “AI-first engineering practices” does not identify the practices or the specific action taken.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what work the contributor did or what skill it demonstrates.

items.says: The broad delivery and downstream benefits lack evidence or a basis for comparison.
items.because: Adoption alone does not establish those effects or show that the practices caused them.

items.says: Going from 900 ms to 600 ms is a 33.3% reduction, not 50%.
items.because: The 300 ms decrease is 33.3% of the starting latency.

items.says: Going from 71% to 83% is an increase of 12 percentage points, not 12%.
“Citation and faithfulness metrics” does not explain how the metrics were built or implemented.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what evaluation skill or technical work the contribution demonstrates.

items.says: The Kendall correlation of 0.89 does not specify the two quantities correlated.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what the correlation demonstrates about the evaluator.

items.says: The result appears after the method.
items.because: The instrumentation appears before the reader learns that the defects were fixed.

items.says: “Each was fixed upstream” does not say who fixed the defects.
items.because: The passive phrasing leaves responsibility for the fixes unclear.
